evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: this is the dissociation of the mass-selected even-electron oxonium ion C2H5O+=CHCH3 (m/z 73), itself generated by EI alpha-cleavage of diethyl ether; not a 70 eV EI reaction of a molecular ion. The 'i' label is a reaction-type mark (i = inductive, rH = H-rearrangement), NOT an electron-pushing arrow (0 arcs drawn). No abundance is printed for this channel (only PA/energy values); product left detected=false, peak status inferred. Eq 8.12, upper ('i') branch of the fork from the even-electron oxocarbenium ion C2H5O(+)=CHCH3 (m/z 73). Inductive (charge-migration) cleavage: the C2-O3 sigma bond breaks heterolytically, both electrons to oxygen, giving the ethyl cation C2H5+ (m/z 29) and neutral acetaldehyde O=CHCH3 (PA = 8.1 eV printed). Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs; the page shows only the net reaction arrow labelled 'i' (inductive) and the product formulae; the single 2-electron move (C2-O3 bonding pair -> O lone pair) is implied by the reaction type, not drawn. No intensity is printed for this channel on the page (unlike Eq 8.10/8.11), so no relative_intensity is asserted; m/z is curator-computed.

Cross-link: MØD rule IMS_8_12 ('Field Rule 8.12 ind', src/data_generation/rules/IMS_chap8_examples.py). VERIFIED MATCH. Its LHS [C]1(H3)[C]5(H2)[O+]8{=}[C]9(H1)[C]11(H3) is exactly this substrate C2H5O(+)=CHCH3 (rule C1=my C1, C5=my C2, O8=my O3, C9=my C4, C11=my C5). RHS cleaves C5-O8, +1 to C5, neutralises O8 keeping O8=C9 -> C2H5+ + O=CHCH3, identical bond changes to this record. Rule fires on this substrate.
